summary: AI capex is generating measurable positive ROIC for hyperscalers, unlike the dot-com era, making the current investment cycle fundamentally different and more sustainable.
summary_extended: Baker argues that the current AI investment cycle is fundamentally different from the dot-com bubble because hyperscalers are generating measurable, positive, and improving ROIC on their AI capex — not destroying capital. He cites Meta specifically as evidence: the company's revenue has accelerated and its ad targeting ROI has improved materially since AI investments began, demonstrating that AI spending is translating into real business outcomes. He contrasts this with the dot-com era, where capital was sunk into dark fiber that sat unutilized for years, whereas today AI GPUs are used so intensively they overheat — a physical signal that demand exceeds supply and capacity is not being wasted. Baker also references Microsoft Copilot adoption statistics as additional evidence of enterprise monetization. The investment implication is that the AI capex cycle is sustainable and that the major hyperscalers investing heavily in AI infrastructure are not in a bubble but rather in a high-ROIC compounding cycle, making them attractive medium-term holdings.
